newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks close shade lower, seen soft.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks close shade lower, seen soft.

text.p: After an initial climb Argentine stocks seesawed lower Wednesday but then recovered most ground, ending with only mild losses.
However, traders expected the market to remain soft as the week draws to a close.

"We had started a correction late yesterday, but it was thwarted by today's sharp rally in New York which pushed us back up," said Rodrigo Diz at Velox Inversiones. "When things calmed down a bit abroad, the bolsa eased again and now every bounce will probably be seen as a chance to take profits."
The blue-chip MerVal index ended down 0.2 percent to 847.24.
"This erratic mode will also be fuelled by end-of-month position squaring," Diz said.
Traders noted market conditions were overbought and trading volumes in the past few sessions were not growing in line with prices.
"Stocks are running out of steam and need to pause," another dealer said. "At these levels we should be very cautious."
Analysts also said the budget deal struck Tuesday in Washington could open up a new era of low bond yields as the U.S. government's financing requirements drop.

"The budget deal spells very good news for the U.S. bond market in the medium and long term," said Miguel Daneri at traders Boston Securities. He predicted the benchmark 30-year Treasury bond yield would aim for a target of five percent.
The long bond yield closed at 6.25 percent Wednesday, its lowest level in nearly a year and a half.
Floor volume totaled 32.4 million pesos on the bolsa, against 34.4 million Tuesday, while over-the-counter turnover picked up to 111.3 million pesos from 90.5 million Tuesday.
The broad market matched MerVal losses of 0.3 percent, but winners still beat losers 31 to 28 and 19 issues ended flat.

Heaviest main-tier losers were pulp and paper maker Celulosa, textile and footwear firm Alpargatas and oil company Astra, off 4.7 percent, 3.4 percent and 2.8 percent, respectively. Best performers were agrochemical firm Atanor, steelmaker Siderar and cement stock Polledo, up 4.9 percent, 3.4 percent and 3.1 percent, respectively.
